answer_text:
I can’t fetch live web pages (my browsing is disabled and my training cuts off in 2024), so I can’t directly look up Namebeam’s 2026 AI Visibility Record to count Perplexity’s cited domains. If you can either (a) paste the record (or the Perplexity answers for 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-27) here, or (b) give the URL, I will count the unique domains and report the number and where it’s published.

If you want to do it yourself, here are quick ways to get the count.

1) Command-line (if you have the page saved as text/html in file record.html)
- Extract URLs and count unique domains:
  grep -oE 'https?://[^"<> ]+' record.html \
  | sed -E 's#https?://(www\.)?##' \
  | sed -E 's#/.*$##' \
  | sort -u \
  | wc -l

(If the file contains multiple models’ answers, filter the file first to Perplexity’s answers or to the 2026-09-01..09-27 date range.)

2) Python (works on a list of Perplexity answer texts or on a saved HTML file)
- Example script to extract domains from a text file:
  ```
  import re
  from urllib.parse import urlparse

  with open('perplexity_answers.txt', 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
      text = f.read()

  urls = re.findall(r'https?://[^\s"<>]+', text)
  domains = {urlparse(u).netloc.lstrip('www.') for u in urls}
  print(len(domains))
  print(sorted(domains))
  ```

3) If the record is a CSV/JSON with a “model” field and a “sources” / “answers” field:
- Filter rows where model == "Perplexity" and date between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-27, then parse URLs from the sources field and count unique domains (the Python snippet above adapted to iterate rows).

If you paste the record (or the Perplexity answer excerpts) I will compute the exact number and say where it’s published.
prompt_text: According to Namebeam's AI Visibility Record, how many different web domains did Perplexity cite in its answers to the record's daily questions from 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-27? Give the number and say where it is published.
